content.value_statement: Manual JSON mapping can produce runtime type errors and duplicated parsing logic. This skill guides type-safe models, HTTP parsing, validation, and isolate usage.
actual_capabilities: Defines immutable Dart model classes that match JSON object fields.
Implements type-safe fromJson factory constructors with explicit validation.
Implements toJson methods that map model properties to JSON keys.
Integrates model parsing with successful HTTP response handling.
Moves large response parsing to a Flutter compute isolate.
Guides unit tests for serialization and type mismatch failures.
limitations: Supports manual serialization for simple models and does not generate code.
Requires developers to define nullability, defaults, and schema-specific validation.
Does not cover authentication, retries, caching, or complete HTTP client design.
Complex nested models need additional mapping logic beyond the provided examples.

use_cases.title: Build a First Flutter API Model
use_cases.description: Create a small immutable model with validated deserialization and predictable serialization.
use_cases.target_user: Flutter developers learning manual JSON mapping

use_cases.title: Integrate Typed HTTP Responses
use_cases.description: Convert successful HTTP response bodies into application models while rejecting invalid status codes.

use_cases.title: Optimize Large Payload Parsing
use_cases.description: Move expensive list decoding into a Flutter isolate to protect interface responsiveness.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Dart model for [fields]. Add a const constructor, fromJson factory, toJson method, and focused unit tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a small JSON object with required scalar fields.

prompt_templates.title: Add Validation
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement manual serialization for [model]. Validate required types and throw FormatException when the input shape is invalid.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when API data must fail clearly on type mismatches.

prompt_templates.title: Parse an HTTP Response
prompt_templates.prompt: Integrate [model] parsing into an injected Dart http client. Check response status, decode safely, and preserve testability.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when connecting a model to a REST endpoint.

prompt_templates.title: Handle a Large Nested Payload
prompt_templates.prompt: Design manual parsing for [payload]. Include nested models, nullable fields, isolate parsing with compute, malformed input tests, and serialization round trips.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for large response arrays with complex model relationships.

output_examples.input: Create a user model with integer identifier, name, and email fields.
output: An immutable User model with required typed fields.
Validated deserialization that rejects missing or incorrect values.

output_examples.input: Parse a large users response without blocking the Flutter interface.
output: A top-level parsing function suitable for a Flutter isolate.
Status validation before decoding the response body.
Typed user list conversion and malformed payload tests.

best_practices: Validate decoded values before constructing models.
Inject HTTP clients so response handling remains testable.
Use compute only when measured parsing work can block a frame.
anti_patterns: Do not trust dynamic decoded values without type checks.
Do not return null for unrelated network and parsing failures.
Do not move small payload parsing to an isolate without measurement.

faq.question: Does this skill use code generation?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on handwritten fromJson and toJson methods for simple data structures.

faq.question: Can it parse JSON from HTTP responses?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows status validation, body decoding, model conversion, and error handling.

faq.question: How are invalid field types handled?
faq.answer: The guidance uses explicit casts or pattern matching and recommends FormatException for invalid object shapes.

faq.question: When should parsing use compute?
faq.answer: Use compute when measured parsing exceeds a frame budget or large payloads cause visible interface delays.

faq.question: Does it support nested and nullable fields automatically?
faq.answer: No. Developers must add model-specific mapping, nullability, defaults, and validation.

faq.question: What tests should accompany a model?
faq.answer: Test valid deserialization, serialization output, round trips, missing fields, incorrect types, and HTTP failures.
